questions.subject: ANALYTICAL_CHEMISTRY
questions.stem: Sample 1001: A buffer has pKa = 8.79 with a conjugate-base to acid concentration ratio of 4.22. What is the buffer pH?

options.misconception: ignores the ratio and reports only the pKa
subtracts the log term instead of adding it
adds the raw ratio rather than its logarithm

questions.explanation: The Henderson-Hasselbalch equation gives pH as pKa plus the logarithm of the base-to-acid ratio. When the ratio is one the pH equals the pKa, but otherwise the log term shifts the pH in the direction of the more abundant species.

provenance.author: bank-team-analychem
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

options.misconception: ignores the ratio and reports only the pKa
subtracts the log term instead of adding it
adds the raw ratio rather than its logarithm

questions.explanation: The Henderson-Hasselbalch equation gives pH as pKa plus the logarithm of the base-to-acid ratio. When the ratio is one the pH equals the pKa, but otherwise the log term shifts the pH in the direction of the more abundant species.

options.misconception: ignores the ratio and reports only the pKa
adds the raw ratio rather than its logarithm
subtracts the log term instead of adding it

questions.explanation: The Henderson-Hasselbalch equation gives pH as pKa plus the logarithm of the base-to-acid ratio. When the ratio is one the pH equals the pKa, but otherwise the log term shifts the pH in the direction of the more abundant species.
